title: Akvan brings heavy rain warning; 1,500 stranded on Saint Martin's
excerpt: Heavy to very heavy rain is forecast for five divisions for 48 hours. The cyclone is expected to make landfall in India on Friday.
content:
The Bangladesh Meteorological Department has forecast heavy to very heavy rain in Rajshahi, Dhaka, Khulna, Barishal and Chattogram divisions for 48 hours from 10am on Thursday (19 November) as Severe Cyclone Akvan moves through the Bay of Bengal, bdnews24.com reported.

About 1,500 tourists are stranded on Saint Martin's Island after ships stopped running on Thursday, the paper said in a separate report.

Where the storm is

At 6am the cyclone was 1,125 km south-west of Chattogram port, with winds of up to 89 kph near the centre, gusting to 117 kph. Local warning signal 3 remains in force at the four seaports and fishing boats have been told to stay in shelter. The storm is expected to cross the northern Andhra Pradesh or southern Odisha coast in India by noon on Friday.

The Cox's Bazar district administration said ship services to Saint Martin's would stay suspended until weather conditions improve. Additional District Magistrate Tasnim Jahan said passenger safety would guide the next decision. Hossain Islam Bahadur, general secretary of the Sea Cruise Operators Owners Association, said people holding Thursday tickets would get refunds if trips could not go ahead, or could use the same tickets later.

Why it matters

Bangladesh is not expected to take a direct hit, but two days of heavy rain in late November could damage standing crops, flood low-lying settlements and keep fishers out of work. Coastal and Rohingya camp programmes may need to check drainage and shelters.

What to watch

Rainfall totals and any landslide warnings for Cox's Bazar and the camps, crop damage reports, and when ship services resume.
